title: Strict-local criterion for constant module direct-image units
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $B$ a finite $\Lambda$-module; write $B_T$ for its constant sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use ordinary derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], inverse image and its adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and bounded-below module and abelian derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For each geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], put $S_{\bar x}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and $Y_{\bar x}^{\mathrm{sh}}=Y\times_XS_{\bar x}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that the constants map
$$B[0]\longrightarrow R\Gamma((Y_{\bar x}^{\mathrm{sh}})_{\mathrm{et}},B_{Y_{\bar x}^{\mathrm{sh}}})$$
is an isomorphism in $D^+(\mathrm{Ab})$ for every $\bar x$, where ordinary sections are [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Then the canonical unit $B_X[0]\to Rf_*B_Y[0]$ is an isomorphism in both the abelian and the fixed-$\Lambda$ module derived categories. Under the canonical restriction identification
$$ (Rf_*B_Y)_{\bar x}\cong R\Gamma((Y_{\bar x}^{\mathrm{sh}})_{\mathrm{et}},B_{Y_{\bar x}^{\mathrm{sh}}}),$$
the stalk of the unit is exactly the constants map in the hypothesis. This criterion includes the empty scheme $X$ and imposes no quasi-compactness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ itself.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images, together with geometric-stalk detection; blueprint Reduction to a geometric fibre, agent unit-normalization and fixed-module refinement.

proof.text: Work first with the underlying abelian group of $B$. Fix $\bar x$, put $Z=Y_{\bar x}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and let $p:Z\to Y$ be the projection. Since $\Lambda$ is finite, two nonnegative multiples of $1$ agree; subtracting gives $n\cdot1=0$ for some $n>0$. Thus $nB=0$, and the zero multiplication-by-$n$ map remains zero after forming the constant sheaf. Hence $B_Y[0]$ has torsion cohomology. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] to $f$ and $B_Y[0]$. Its hypotheses require only that $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, as assumed. Applying [lem-kun-pullback-constant] to $p$ identifies $p^{-1}B_Y$ with $B_Z$. This gives the canonical restriction isomorphism $c_{\bar x}:(Rf_*B_Y)_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Z,B_Z)$ in the statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], $B\to(B_X)_{\bar x}$ is the specific isomorphism sending a coefficient to its constant germ.

source.place: Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), canonical restriction in the last proof paragraph; Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact).

proof.text: We check the map, not just its source and target. Compute $Rf_*$ by an injective resolution $j:B_Y[0]\to I^\bullet$ as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. By the inverse-image adjunction [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], the derived unit is represented by $B_X[0]\to f_*B_Y[0]\to f_*I^\bullet$, where the first map sends a constant coefficient to that same constant on each $Y\times_XV$. A coefficient $b\in B$ represents its stalk class on the pointed neighbourhood $(X,\bar x)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]. The canonical restriction of [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] is induced by restricting sections on $Y\times_XV$ to $Z$, followed by the comparison to derived sections. For $V=X$, this sends $j(b)$ to its pullback on $Z$. The canonical comparison of [lem-kun-pullback-constant] sends the pulled-back constant $b$ to the constant $b$ in $B_Z$. Thus the composite $B[0]\to(B_X[0])_{\bar x}\to(Rf_*B_Y)_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{c_{\bar x}}R\Gamma(Z,B_Z)$ is the constants map: before localization both constructions send $b$ to the same degree-zero cocycle and have zero components in all other degrees. This is equality of the derived morphisms themselves.

source.place: Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), canonical restriction in the last proof paragraph; Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact).

proof.text: The hypothesis makes the composite in step 2 invertible. Its outer identifications are invertible by step 1, so the abelian unit is invertible at every geometric stalk. Exactness of the stalk functor [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identifies cohomology of its stalk with the stalks of its cohomology-sheaf maps. Consequently all these maps are invertible, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] proves that $B_X[0]\to Rf_*B_Y[0]$ is an isomorphism in the abelian derived category.

source.place: Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), canonical restriction in the last proof paragraph; Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact).

proof.text: For module coefficients let $U_T$ forget scalars. The constant-section comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-coefficients], applied to the identity of $T$, identifies $U_T(B_T)$ with the abelian constant sheaf just used. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison], $U_T$ is exact and its canonical derived direct-image comparison is invertible and unit-compatible. Therefore forgetting the module unit, and then applying this comparison, gives precisely the abelian unit of step 3. To reflect invertibility, note that exactness gives $U_X\mathcal H^i=\mathcal H^iD^+(U_X)$ by applying $U_X$ to kernels, images and their quotients. Each forgotten cohomology map is consequently invertible. The inverse of an invertible underlying additive sheaf map is linear: if $h$ is linear and bijective on sections, $h^{-1}(a n)=a h^{-1}(n)$ follows by applying $h$; its inverse also commutes with restrictions. Thus every module cohomology map is invertible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] in the module abelian category to conclude that the module unit is an isomorphism.

No argument imposed a condition on $X$ beyond being a scheme: the stalk formula only required the given conditions on $f$. If $X$ is empty, its family of geometric points is empty and the same derived-stalk conservativity criterion still applies, so the conclusion holds. Concretely a sheaf of abelian groups or modules on the empty etale site has zero sections by the empty covering, so both derived categories are zero. The constants calculation also holds when $B=0$ or $Z$ is empty; in the latter case the hypothesis forces $B=0$ if that geometric point occurs.

lean.statement: theorem strictLocal_constant_unit_criterion {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] (B : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) [Finite B] (h : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X), IsIso (constantDerivedSectionsMap AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (pullback f (Scheme.strictLocalizationToBase x)) ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj B))) : IsIso (constantDerivedDirectImageUnit AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj B)) ∧ IsIso (constantDerivedDirectImageUnit (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f B) ∧ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X), ∃ r : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ≅ upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (Scheme.strictLocalizationToBase x) ⋙ Sheaf.Γ (Scheme.strictLocalization x).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}, (∀ F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}, IsStrictHenselizationStalkRestriction x F (r.hom.app F)) ∧ IsIso (strictLocalConstantDerivedRestriction f x r ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj B)) ∧ constantDerivedGeometricGerm ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj B) x ≫ (constantUnitDerivedStalk x).map (constantDerivedDirectImageUnit AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj B)) ≫ strictLocalConstantDerivedRestriction f x r ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj B) = constantDerivedSectionsMap AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (pullback f (Scheme.strictLocalizationToBase x)) ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj B)
lean.note: The six helper declarations specialize recorded functors and canonical comparison maps. The restriction parameter is a natural isomorphism uniquely pinned on every representative germ by IsStrictHenselizationStalkRestriction, asserted to exist in the conclusion; it is not an arbitrary identification or an added hypothesis. The normalization is an equality in D+(Ab), not just an equality on cohomology. No statement correction or new mathematical notion.
